name: Fine Arts
description: Painting, sculpture, classical music and the artists behind them.

lessons.title: Renaissance Painters
lessons.body:
The **Renaissance** (“rebirth”) began in Italy in the 1400s.

- **Leonardo da Vinci** painted the **Mona Lisa** (in the Louvre, Paris) and **The Last Supper** (on a wall in Milan). He also filled notebooks with inventions and anatomy drawings.
- **Michelangelo** painted the **Sistine Chapel ceiling**, including *The Creation of Adam*, and sculpted **David** and the **Pietà**.
- **Raphael** painted **The School of Athens**, showing Plato and Aristotle at the center.
- **Sandro Botticelli** painted **The Birth of Venus**, where the goddess stands on a scallop shell.

**Tip:** link each artist to one painting and one city.
keyFacts: The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre in Paris.
The Last Supper is a wall painting in Milan.
Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling and sculpted David.
Raphael painted The School of Athens.
Botticelli’s Venus stands on a scallop shell.

lessons.title: Great Composers
lessons.body:
Classical music questions often name a famous piece and ask for the composer.

- **Johann Sebastian Bach** (Baroque): the *Brandenburg Concertos*.
- **Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart** (Classical): child prodigy from Salzburg; operas *The Magic Flute* and *The Marriage of Figaro*.
- **Ludwig van Beethoven**: kept composing after going deaf. His **Symphony No. 5** begins “da-da-da-DUM,” and his **Symphony No. 9** ends with the “Ode to Joy.”
- **Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky**: the ballets *Swan Lake* and *The Nutcracker*, and the *1812 Overture* with real cannons.
- **Antonio Vivaldi**: *The Four Seasons*, four violin concertos.
keyFacts: Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony ends with the “Ode to Joy.”
Beethoven went deaf but kept composing.
Tchaikovsky wrote The Nutcracker and Swan Lake.
Mozart was born in Salzburg, Austria.

tossups.question: This artist complained that he was a sculptor, not a painter, when the pope gave him a huge painting job. He carved the Pietà, and he painted God reaching toward Adam on the Sistine Chapel ceiling. For 10 points, name this Italian artist who sculpted David.

This composer wrote a piano piece called “Für Elise.” He was almost totally deaf when his Ninth Symphony, featuring the “Ode to Joy,” was first performed. For 10 points, name this German composer of a Fifth Symphony that begins with four famous notes.

bonuses.leadin: Name these composers from one of their works, for 10 points each.
